stem:
Muttley Magee is an 8-year-old boy with asthma. He has had asthma attacks every month over winter and was discharged from the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) a few days ago after a severe attack. He has been off oxygen since yesterday. He has also had a history of waking at night at least 5 days every week. He complains of wheezing with exercise and needs to take his ventolin at least once a day.

Which of the following best describes Muttley's asthma?
explanation: Muttley has very frequent night-time symptoms, daily reliever use, exercise limitation, and a recent severe exacerbation requiring PICU admission. This pattern is most consistent with severe persistent asthma.
rationale: Severe persistent asthma is the best fit because symptom frequency and recent ICU-level exacerbation indicate poor control and high severity.

optionExplanations.A: Intermittent asthma would have infrequent symptoms and minimal night waking, which is not the case here.
optionExplanations.B: Frequent intermittent asthma is less severe than this child’s daily and nocturnal symptoms.
optionExplanations.C: Mild persistent asthma does not fit the frequency of symptoms or recent severe exacerbation.
optionExplanations.D: Moderate persistent asthma is still less severe than the combination of daily symptoms and frequent nocturnal waking.
optionExplanations.E: Correct: the child has daily symptoms, frequent night waking, exercise-induced symptoms, and a recent life-threatening exacerbation.
